issues.title: Idle detection misses legitimate input events
issues.description: IdleMonitor checks a hand-maintained subset of CoreGraphics event types and omits events such as mouse dragging, mouse button release, and tablet input. Active users could therefore be classified as idle. Replace the event array and map/min scan with CoreGraphics' single any-input-event query.

issues.title: Session lock and display sleep are not handled
issues.description: BreakScheduler observes full system sleep but not session resignation, screen locking, or display sleep. A break countdown can continue while the user is locked out or away, then begin a new work interval before they return. Handle the relevant workspace notifications and reset the interval when the user returns after sufficient time away.

issues.title: Break overlay does not explicitly restore application focus
issues.description: OverlayController force-activates Twenty to make its buttons interactive, but it does not save or restore the previously active application after the overlay closes. Focus restoration is left to incidental AppKit behavior. Capture the previous frontmost application and restore or yield activation when the break ends.

issues.title: Launch-at-login UI reduces a four-state API to a stale Boolean
issues.description: SettingsView treats SMAppService status as enabled or disabled, ignoring requiresApproval and notFound. The value is initialized once, is not refreshed when the persistent settings window reappears, and registration errors are silently swallowed. Refresh the status when shown, represent approval-required state, provide a path to Login Items settings, and display actionable errors.

issues.title: Break countdown measures timer callbacks instead of elapsed time
issues.description: OverlayController subtracts one second for each timer callback. If the main run loop stalls, the configured break lasts longer than intended. Store an end deadline and derive the remaining time from the current time on every callback.

issues.title: Using Later during a manual paused break silently resumes reminders
issues.description: When a user starts a manual break while reminders are paused, completed and skipped outcomes preserve the pause, but Later schedules a snoozed reminder and cancels the paused state. This is surprising for a feature named Pause Reminders. Preserve the previous paused state for every manual-break outcome unless product behavior explicitly says otherwise.

issues.title: Persisted settings are not validated or clamped
issues.description: AppSettings trusts raw UserDefaults values even though values can come from old versions, command-line defaults changes, corruption, or future migrations. Zero or extreme values can trigger immediate repeated overlays or excessively long breaks. Centralize allowed ranges and clamp values when reading them.

issues.title: Core scheduling state machine has no automated tests
issues.description: The package has no test target, and BreakScheduler directly depends on Date, Timer, IdleMonitor, UserDefaults, workspace notifications, and the real overlay. Add small test seams and deterministic coverage for pause and resume, manual breaks, snooze, idle return, short and long sleep, session locking, settings changes, and overlay completion races.

issues.title: Custom settings controls have insufficient accessibility metadata
issues.description: The work interval slider, launch-at-login switch, and plus/minus controls lack useful setting-specific accessibility labels and values. VoiceOver users may hear generic control names without context. Prefer native labeled controls or add explicit accessibility labels, values, and hints; also consider keyboard shortcuts for Later and Skip.

issues.title: Build script has portability and release-process gaps
issues.description: The build script assumes the SwiftPM binary is under .build/<configuration>, uses a narrow hard-coded Xcode lookup, generates an actool partial plist without consuming it, and supports only ad-hoc signing. Use swift build --show-bin-path, discover actool through the selected developer tools, either merge or remove the partial plist, and define real signing, hardened-runtime, and notarization steps for distribution.

issues.title: Menu status formatting unexpectedly mutates scheduler state
issues.description: BreakScheduler.menuStatusText starts a new work session when called while waiting for return. A formatting/query method should not perform a state transition. Move return detection to an explicit action and keep status formatting read-only.

issues.title: Overlay window frame is set twice
issues.description: OverlayController initializes each window with screen.frame and then calls setFrame with the same frame. Remove the redundant setFrame call unless a documented AppKit behavior requires it.

issues.title: Overlay window release configuration is unnecessary
issues.description: Overlay windows set isReleasedWhenClosed to false even though they are never closed; they are ordered out and released through the controller's array. Remove the setting to reduce irrelevant lifecycle configuration.

issues.title: Secure restorable state callback appears unnecessary
issues.description: AppDelegate implements applicationSupportsSecureRestorableState even though the menu-bar app does not implement window restoration. Remove it unless restoration support is intentionally planned and tested.

issues.title: Icon geometry has multiple sources of truth
issues.description: The horizon-gaze mark is independently encoded in AppKit drawing code, SwiftUI Canvas code, and SVG assets. These copies can drift. Prefer one reusable asset or shared geometry representation where practical.

issues.title: README understates the required SwiftPM version
issues.description: The README says Swift 6 is required, while Package.swift declares swift-tools-version 6.2. Update the documented requirement to Swift 6.2 or later.

issues.title: Development environment overrides are incompletely documented
issues.description: TWENTY_IDLE_RESET_SECONDS and TWENTY_SNOOZE_SECONDS are supported in code but omitted from the README. Document all supported development overrides in one place.

issues.title: Work interval override conflicts with live settings changes
issues.description: When TWENTY_WORK_SECONDS is active, changing the work interval setting causes BreakScheduler to recalculate the pending deadline in minutes, bypassing the development override. Either ignore settings changes while the override is active or consistently derive the recalculated interval through AppSettings.workInterval.
